title: Mattie Lee Boyd
text:
[Photograph: a young woman in a long dress standing outdoors on rocky ground, holding a bow and arrow.]

MATTIE LEE BOYD

The author of Part I of this book refused to permit the use of her photograph therein, and the use of her picture here is unauthorized by her. The publishers believe, however, that those who receive the book will appreciate knowing how she looks; and, again, this is another evidence on their part of their sincere admiration of her work. The bow she is holding was a gift from old Indian students of the school. It is unstrung. That is the Indian's way of denoting peace. The turkey feather on the end of the arrow means friendship, morality and brotherly love. This bow has been placed in the archives of the Association as a sacred relic.
notes: Photograph and note about the author Mattie Lee Boyd; the bow she holds was a gift from former Indian students of the college.
